questions.text: In vector notation, a force is written as **F** = 12**i** − 8**j** kN. Which property is conveyed by the negative sign on the **j** component?

options.text: The magnitude in the y-direction is negative, indicating a reversal of direction compared to positive values.
The sense in the y-direction is downward
The direction is horizontal, which is a misunderstanding of vector components.
The overall magnitude is negative, which is incorrect as only the direction is affected.

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The negative sign on the **j** component (−8**j**) indicates that the y-direction component points downward, opposing the positive y-axis. This is sense—the orientation. The magnitude of this component is still 8 kN (positive).
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three fundamental properties of a force?

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The three properties of a force are magnitude, direction, and sense. Duration (how long the force is applied) is not a defining property of the force itself—it affects load combinations but not the force's inherent character.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A structural analyst needs to fully specify a force acting on a beam to a construction team. Which combination of information is necessary and sufficient?

options.text: Magnitude and direction only, assuming uniform material properties and load distribution
Direction and sense only, which are critical for understanding force application
Magnitude and sense only, focusing on the intensity and orientation of the force

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: All three properties—magnitude (the number), direction (the line of action), and sense (the arrow orientation)—are necessary to completely and unambiguously define a force. Without any one, the specification is incomplete or ambiguous.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A 25 kN force acts at 60° from the horizontal. Which statement is true about this force's properties?

options.text: Its sense is undefined without an arrow
All three properties are fully specified

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The phrase 'at 60° from horizontal' specifies the direction—the line of action. Magnitude is 25 kN. Sense requires an arrowhead on the diagram to show which of the two possible ways along the 60° line the force points.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: In Philippine structural practice, a load specification reads: 'A dead load of 2.5 kN/m² is applied to the floor slab.' Identify which property of individual forces this load DOES NOT explicitly specify.

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: A downward load due to gravity is the standard assumption in Philippine strucorrect_option_id should be 'c' (Sense). Sense (downward) is NOT explicitly stated in the load description—it is only implied by the convention that dead loads act downward due to gravity. To be fully explicit, the specification should state: 2.5 kN/m² acting downward (perpendicular to slab).'ecification gives magnitude (2.5 kN/m²) and direction (perpendicular to slab). questions.text: A force of 15 kN acting horizontally to the right and a force of 15 kN acting horizontally to the left differ in which property or properties?

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Both forces have the same magnitude (15 kN) and the same direction (horizontal line of action). They differ only in sense: one points right, the other left.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: In a free-body diagram, a vertical downward arrow labeled '20 kN' represents a force. Which property is indicated by the downward direction of the arrow?

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The downward arrow indicates sense—the specific orientation (up or down) along the vertical line of action. The vertical line itself represents the direction (the line of action); the numerical label (20 kN) is the magnitude. Note: In a free-body diagram, the arrow symbol inherently communicates both direction (via its position/orientation) and sense (via its arrowhead), so option 'd' could be defended; however, the most precise answer is 'c' because sense is the distinguishing property the arrow adds to the line of action.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: On a structural drawing, you see a downward arrow at a column base labeled '500 kN.' What does the label '500 kN' represent?

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The numerical value '500 kN' is the magnitude—the intensity or size of the force. The downward arrow gives the sense; the vertical line gives the direction.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Two forces act on a beam: Force A is 30 kN downward; Force B is 30 kN upward. The structural effects of these forces on the beam will be:

options.text: Identical, since both have the same magnitude
Opposite, since they differ in sense
Opposite, since they differ in direction

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The structural effects are opposite because the forces differ in sense. Force A pushes down; Force B pushes up. Although they share magnitude and direction, their opposite sense means they produce opposite effects—one creates tension at the bottom, the other at the top.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: An engineer describes a force as 'acting downward along a vertical column.' Which of the three fundamental properties is NOT explicitly stated in this description?

rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The description specifies direction ('along a vertical column') and sense ('downward'). The magnitude—the numerical value—is missing.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.
